patient.chief_complaint: Two-year progressive disinhibition and personality change in a retired military officer.
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. F. is a 64-year-old right-handed White retired military officer referred for evaluation of progressive personality change over 2 years. A decorated officer known for his strict discipline and professionalism, he has undergone a dramatic personality transformation. He resigned from his second career in real estate 2 years ago after making a sexual remark to a client. Since then, his behavior has escalated: he makes explicit sexual comments to female neighbors, gets into confrontations at grocery stores, and once exposed himself to family members during a gathering. He has developed compulsive military-themed rituals — rearranging his medals and memorabilia in precise order for hours each day. His appetite has become voracious. His alcohol use has escalated from rare to 4-6 beers daily. He shows complete lack of insight, stating he is 'just more relaxed now.' His wife is terrified and has removed firearms from the home after he made an impulsive comment about shooting a neighbor's dog. No family history of dementia. He cannot tolerate MRI because of severe claustrophobia and has declined sedation.

findings.domain: Dysexecutive profile with relative sparing of memory and visuospatial

clinical_assessment.impression: 4 of the six Rascovsky behavioural features are documented, against the three required for possible behavioural-variant frontotemporal dementia, alongside a dysexecutive bedside profile. The diagnosis is behavioural and is made on this assessment; imaging supports it and does not substitute for it. Memory and visuospatial function are relatively spared, which is the discriminator against Alzheimer's disease and the reason a screening total alone understates the syndrome.

results.title: Firearms and dementia
results.finding: People with FTD have markedly increased risk of impulsive, violent behavior; firearms in home represent serious safety hazard

output.summary: Patients with frontotemporal dementia have markedly increased risk of impulsive behavior secondary to orbitofrontal and ventromedial prefrontal dysfunction. Published literature documents elevated risk of impulsive violent acts in this population. Firearms access in the home of a patient with frontal disinhibition has been identified in the literature as a significant safety hazard requiring clinical attention.

tool_parameters.query: Frontotemporal dementia diagnostic criteria and management

useless_tools.rationale: EEG is non-specific in FTD; not part of the standard dementia workup unless seizures or rapidly progressive course suggest CJD or autoimmune encephalitis.
ECG has no role in the cognitive workup of suspected FTD; reserved for syncope, palpitations, or pre-procedure clearance.
Echocardiography is unrelated to a neurodegenerative cognitive syndrome and adds cost without diagnostic value.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is unrelated to FTD and not indicated absent syncope or palpitations.
MR spectroscopy has no established role in the routine FTD diagnostic pathway.
Perfusion MRI is not indicated in the standard FTD workup once a structural MRI and FDG-PET (or amyloid PET) have characterised the lobar pattern.
Carotid duplex is a vascular study with no diagnostic role in primary neurodegenerative dementia.
DaTscan evaluates presynaptic dopaminergic terminals; it is not indicated unless overt parkinsonism raises concern for PD, DLB, or atypical parkinsonism (PSP/CBS overlap).

harmful_tools.rationale: MRI is unavailable after failed preparation for severe claustrophobia and the patient declines sedation; use non-contrast CT and state its limitations

critical_actions: Apply Rascovsky 2011 bvFTD criteria explicitly (≥3 of 6 core features within 3 years) and document functional decline.
Assess and document decision-making, financial, and driving capacity given the high risk of impulsivity and impaired judgment in FTD.
Provide caregiver education, safety planning, and referral to FTD-focused support resources.
Offer genetic counselling and discuss cascade testing options if a pathogenic variant is identified or suspected.
contraindicated_actions: Do not start acetylcholinesterase inhibitors (donepezil, rivastigmine, galantamine): no benefit in FTD and may worsen behavioral symptoms.
Do not start memantine: no evidence of benefit in bvFTD and may worsen behavioral symptoms.
Avoid antipsychotics as first-line behavioral therapy given increased cerebrovascular and mortality risk in dementia; reserve for refractory dangerous agitation with specialist oversight.
Avoid benzodiazepines for behavioral control: risk of paradoxical disinhibition and falls.
key_reasoning_points: Rascovsky bvFTD criteria met with imaging confirmation.
Document any prior head trauma but degenerative imaging pattern is not CTE-specific.
Mild rigidity is not parkinsonism warranting DaTscan.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Mild rigidity is common in advanced bvFTD; DaTscan is not indicated.
